summary: Paul's allegory of Sarah and Hagar sets two covenants side by side. Hagar and Ishmael stand for the law, works and self-effort, born when Abraham and Sarah rushed God's promise. Sarah and Isaac stand for grace through faith, born free by promise. Every other religion, and some that carry the Christian name, tells people to work for a salvation they can never be sure of, while the gospel rests on what Christ has already done. Scripture shows God delivering in ways only he can explain, and sometimes asking us to wait. Trusting his timing means working alongside him, not forcing his hand.
takeaways: There are only two kinds of religion: one built on what Christ has done, and every other kind built on what we must do.
Ishmael stands for law, works and self-effort, born when Abraham and Sarah took God's promise into their own hands.
Isaac stands for grace through faith, born free by God's promise, means, timing and terms. New Testament believers live under that covenant of promise.
Pushing ahead of God's timing brings chaos, while God often delivers in ways we cannot explain or take credit for, so that they point to him alone.
Trusting God is a process: wait on his timing, work alongside him, and stand firm, because our labor in the Lord is not in vain.
